name: Real-Time Mapping Runtime
description: A dedicated DirectInput-to-vJoy worker owns report processing so controller output is not scheduled by the UI.
subfeatures: Independent mapping worker with a bounded target report rate and UI snapshots published separately.
Precompiled mapping state swapped between reports rather than rebuilt inside the hot path.
Change-driven vJoy writes for stationary inputs and stable idle behavior.
Safe reset/quiesce behavior on Mapping Off, controller disconnect, or output invalidation.
Fresh physical snapshot seeding after reconnect to avoid synthetic button edges.

name: Axis Routing and Processing
description: Physical DirectInput axes can be routed to available vJoy axes with profile-owned transforms and labels.
subfeatures: Runtime discovery of vJoy X, Y, Z, Rx, Ry, Rz, Slider 0, and Slider 1 targets.
Per-profile axis routing with conflict prevention and unsupported-target handling.
Calibration and normalization before profile transforms.
Rescaled deadzone, hysteresis, inversion, response curve, and output-limit processing.
Centered or One-Sided axis domain selectable per profile and per axis.
Direct decimal Output Min/Max entry with 0.1% step adjustment.
Per-profile custom physical-axis names and game-facing virtual-axis aliases.
Global Disabled Axis Value from -100.0% to +100.0% for parked unclaimed outputs.

name: Mapping Safety Controls
description: Mapping state can be controlled without tearing down the physical device, while virtual outputs are forced to deliberate neutral states.
subfeatures: Global Mapping On, Mapping Off, and Toggle Mapping physical-button controls.
Equivalent Mapping On/Off/Toggle actions available to Automation.
Press-edge handling prevents a held button from repeatedly toggling mapping.
Mapping Off centers exposed virtual axes, releases virtual buttons, and centers continuous/discrete POVs.
UI status distinguishes active mapping, mapping off, and missing-device suspension.

name: Button Mapping
description: Physical buttons are discovered from the active controller and routed to available vJoy buttons with explicit ownership.
subfeatures: One-to-one default passthrough for newly discovered buttons while virtual capacity is available.
Explicit Disabled state that remains persistent and is not overwritten by later auto-initialization.
Destination uniqueness avoids ambiguous releases from multiple physical sources.
Press-to-identify and live physical/output state in the UI.
Per-profile custom physical-button names.
Profile-control or mapping-control buttons are consumed from normal vJoy routing while their saved routes remain intact.

name: POV / Hat Support
description: DirectInput POV hats can act as discrete logical directions, profile controls, or native vJoy POV outputs.
subfeatures: Diagnostics support for up to four physical hats with raw angle and logical direction reporting.
Eight logical directions per hat for button-style routing.
Direct native vJoy continuous POV passthrough preserving raw angle.
Discrete vJoy POV output with documented cardinal fallback for diagonals.
POV directions can trigger global Profile Hold or Profile Toggle controls.
Native POV targets are kept separate from direction-as-button routing to avoid accidental overlap.

name: Profiles
description: Profiles package axis and button behavior into instant-switching configurations without reacquiring DirectInput or vJoy.
subfeatures: Persistent base profiles with create, clone/start-from, rename, delete, and live activation.
New profiles are deep copies with no live parent link.
Profile-owned routes, deadzones, hysteresis, inversion, domains, limits, curves, button routes, and custom names.
Global physical-button and POV Profile Hold/Toggle controls.
Deterministic precedence: newest active Hold, then newest active Toggle, then manual base profile.
Manual profile selection clears Toggle overrides while currently held Hold controls remain until release.
Stop Mapping and disconnect clear runtime-only profile overrides.

name: Response Curves
description: Each profile/axis can use compiled response curves with both preset-based and point-based editing.
subfeatures: Linear, J-Curve, and S-Curve families.
Eight standard strengths plus ten evidence-informed Advanced Presets.
Reusable Personal Presets with save/manage workflows.
Optional point editing with Smooth PCHIP-style or Linear interpolation.
5, 7, 9, 13, 17, and 25-point materialization with nonuniform placement support.
Point add/remove, locks, snapping, keyboard nudges, and local undo/redo.
Large live dual-curve viewer with physical/final markers, reference/output traces, gain view, comparison/audition overlays, zoom/pan, cursor inspection, and signal-path visibility.
Immutable 4097-sample response LUTs compiled when configuration changes so editable point count does not affect runtime lookup resolution.

name: Automation Engine
description: A deterministic, fixed-capacity Automation subsystem evaluates rules inside the mapper using data compiled before report processing.
subfeatures: Up to 64 rules with up to four requirements and four effects per rule.
Physical axis, button, POV, profile, and Always requirements.
AND/OR matching with plain-language summaries instead of exposing engine enum terminology to normal users.
Axis threshold hysteresis and crosses-above/crosses-below events.
Button pressed, released, long-press, and two-to-five press sequence triggers.
Momentary, rule-toggle, and timed rule behavior.
vJoy Button Hold, Toggle, and bounded Tap actions.
Profile Hold and Toggle actions.
Axis Scale, Offset, Clamp, Override, Mix, and Follow actions.
Mapping On, Mapping Off, and Toggle Mapping actions.
Per-rule timing for sequence gap, long press, brief active duration, and tap duration.
Runtime latch/timer state is bounded, nonpersistent, and cleared on mapping stop, disconnect, configuration replacement, or Automation master disable.
Global persisted Automation master kill switch, invalid-rule health, and evaluation diagnostics.

name: Automation Editor UX
description: Automation is edited as readable full-page rules rather than raw condition/action arrays.
subfeatures: Dedicated full-page editor for each automation.
New rules are blank, disabled drafts that cannot affect output until valid and saved.
WHEN SHOULD THIS HAPPEN? and WHAT SHOULD IT DO? builders use ordinary HOTAS language.
All the time is represented as a rule-level user choice while legacy Always terms are normalized behind the scenes.
Live RULE SUMMARY explains the draft before save.
Priority and timing controls are placed under Advanced when appropriate.
Overview cards show readable WHEN/DO summaries and Momentary/Toggle/Timed behavior labels.
Unsaved-change handling and delete confirmation.

name: Diagnostics and Observability
description: The application exposes physical input, transformed output, capacity, readiness, and runtime state without making diagnostics part of the output path.
subfeatures: Live axis, button, POV, and virtual-output visualization.
Scrollable bounded event log.
Physical update age and live/stale state.
vJoy readiness, button capacity, axis availability, and POV capability reporting.
HidHide installation/cloaking status when the supported CLI can answer.
Automation rule count, active count, invalid health, and evaluation timing.
Actual parked disabled-axis output reported separately from raw physical input.
Configuration warnings for capability mismatch or unavailable targets.

name: User Interface and Themes
description: The app provides three persistent visual systems without allowing presentation state to alter mapping semantics.
subfeatures: Legacy theme preserving the v1.6.3 presentation.
Standard theme as the modern general-purpose interface.
Top Gun theme with naval-instrument surfaces, aviation-orange actions, brass/ivory/cyan telemetry accents, fighter artwork, wing badge, technical stripes, and themed footer/header treatments.
Instant theme switching with theme state stored separately from mapper configuration.
Dedicated pages for Home, Axes, Buttons, Curves, Diagnostics, Settings, Profiles, and Automation.
Shared themed selectors, numeric inputs, dialogs, cards, and status controls.
Embedded application icon used by the mapper, launcher, installer, shortcuts, and in-app surfaces.

name: vJoy Integration
description: vJoy is dynamically loaded and queried so the application adapts to the virtual device actually configured on the machine.
subfeatures: Dynamic x64 vJoyInterface.dll loading with no vendored SDK binary dependency.
Runtime axis, button, continuous POV, and discrete POV capability discovery.
Safe handling of insufficient button capacity and unavailable axis targets.
Open Configure vJoy action for user-controlled device setup.
No automatic rewriting of an already configured vJoy device.

name: HidHide and Dependency Bootstrap
description: The application helps establish the surrounding controller stack while leaving privileged configuration under user control.
subfeatures: Detection of vJoy and HidHide presence.
Pinned official dependency installers may be offered only when a dependency is missing.
Dependency payload SHA-256 and Authenticode verification before vendor installers are opened.
No silent update, downgrade, enable, cloak, or reconfiguration of an already-installed dependency.
Direct action to open the HidHide Configuration Client.

name: Launcher, Installer, and Updates
description: A native launcher owns stable update checks and installation handoff so network/update work never remains active during mapping.
subfeatures: Console-free native Win32 launcher using WinHTTP and Windows CNG SHA-256.
Stable-release-only update manifest lookup with short timeouts.
Downloaded installer checksum verification before silent handoff.
Failure-safe fallback to the currently installed mapper when update checks, downloads, validation, or installer handoff fail.
Per-user Inno Setup installation under LocalAppData with Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts.
Existing QSettings profiles, curves, calibration, and controls are preserved across program upgrades.
In-app update availability indicator and Settings update action hand off to the already-installed launcher.

name: Configuration and Migration
description: Persistent configuration evolves through explicit schema migrations while transient runtime state remains outside saved data.
subfeatures: QSettings-backed persistent profiles and global settings.
Schema migrations preserve established behavior for older configurations.
Automation schema defaults new temporal fields deterministically.
Profile IDs remain stable for controls and readable summaries use profile names.
Runtime-only toggles, latches, timers, and held-control state are never persisted.

name: Build, Test, and Release Engineering
description: The repository contains a reproducible Windows build and release pipeline intended to catch both correctness and packaging regressions.
subfeatures: Single HOTAS_VERSION authority used by the app, launcher, installer, manifest, and tag validation.
CMake/C++20 build with Qt 6.5+.
Headless mapping, automation, launcher, and configuration tests.
Synthetic mapping hot-path benchmark in release validation.
QML linting and resource/icon checks.
Dependency metadata validation.
Qt deployment staging, installer compilation, install/uninstall smoke test, checksums, update manifest generation, and GitHub Release publication.
Optional Authenticode signing hooks when signing credentials are configured.
